spots.s: 1,200 acres of gardens, 17 museums, and Spanish Colonial architecture — the single best date reservoir in the city.
The world-famous one actually earns it — go at opening, do the canyon loops before the crowds.
Koi ponds, bonsai, and a quiet canyon stroll inside Balboa Park — tailor-made for a slow-conversation date.
A full aircraft carrier on the Embarcadero with 30 restored aircraft — genuinely great even if museums aren't your thing.
One of baseball's best parks; grab Park at the Park lawn tickets and split fish tacos behind center field.
Flat bayfront stroll from the Midway to the Convention Center — harbor lights, street musicians, easy first-date pacing.
A swaying 1912 footbridge over a canyon in Bankers Hill — free, five minutes, and a guaranteed conversation.

spots.n: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
spots.s: Birthplace-of-California adobes, mariachi patios, and fresh tortillas at Café Coyote — cheerfully touristy but fun.
Former Navy mess hall at Liberty Station packed with local vendors — graze, then walk the waterfront art district.
Saturdays 8a–2p on West Date St — one of the country's best markets; espresso, oysters, and people-watching for blocks.
Golden-hour cliff walk above crashing surf in Point Loma — the city's default great-date closer.
Sweeping bay-and-skyline view up top, winter low-tide pools below — check the tide chart before you go.
A $8-ish, 15-minute hop across the bay to Coronado Ferry Landing — rent bikes on the other side; skyline views both ways.
Walk the wide white-sand beach past the 1888 Victorian, then drinks at the Del's beachfront bar — timeless date material.
Ride the 1925 Giant Dipper coaster, then join the rollerbladers and cruisers on the oceanfront boardwalk.
Sea lions barking on the rocks and 30-foot-visibility snorkeling in the ecological reserve — bring or rent a mask.
Bluff-top trails through the rarest pine in North America, dropping to an empty state beach — best easy hike in the county.
Watch paragliders launch off 300-foot cliffs over Black's Beach with coffee from the shack — free show, big wow factor.
360° panorama from La Jolla to Mexico — the drive-up sunset view when you want the city at your feet.
Scripps Oceanography's cliff-top aquarium — seadragons, a big kelp tank, and a patio view over the Pacific; sneaky-good date.

nightlife.s: Underground Gaslamp room that plays actual hip-hop and R&B Thursday through Sunday — reggae Sundays are the sleeper.
615 Broadway's big-production room — LED walls, hip-hop and open-format headliners Fridays and Saturdays.
Three stories plus a 400-person rooftop; EDM-leaning main room with hip-hop nights sprinkled through the calendar.
Three rooms, three sounds — open-format main floor, reggaeton bar, and the intimate Grotto; easy to find your lane.
22 floors above the Gaslamp with Petco Park and bay views — DJs on weekends, conversation-friendly early.
Fifth Ave rooftop with craft cocktails and a heated patio — ideal pre-club dinner-and-drinks staging ground.
North Park whiskey library with live jazz, funk, and soul most nights — a grown-up room where you can actually talk.
Basement 1920s room under Fifth Ave with live jazz and blues nightly — no phones on the floor, which keeps it social.
Reservation-worthy rum temple hidden inside Craft & Commerce — flaming mugs and one of the best bar teams in town.
Walk through a fake liquor-store wall at UTC into a rotating-fireplace parlor — pure theater, great for impressing a date.
The legendary 200-cap rock room since 1989 — Nirvana played here; check the calendar and take a chance on a band.
Three-level Little Italy venue heavy on R&B, soul, funk, and tribute nights — dinner tables downstairs, dance floor up.
Unpretentious warehouse-style club in Middletown for proper house and techno — for when you want to dance, not pose.
Pacific Beach's sprawling indoor-outdoor party — hip-hop and top-40 rooms, fire pits, and zero dress code.
Private K-pop-style karaoke suites on Convoy with Korean fried chicken and soju cocktails — book a room, bring the crew.
Gaslamp dueling-piano institution — request-driven singalongs that turn a room of strangers into one loud choir.

eats.s: Yukito Ota's Pacific Beach strip-mall legend — the omakase and dry-aged tuna that trained a generation of SD chefs.
Michelin one-star Edomae counter near Old Town — the most serious sushi in the city and it still takes some walk-ins.
Chef Soichi Kadoya's eight-seat University Heights counter — ~16 courses of nigiri-forward omakase, two seatings a night.
Bankers Hill's intimate omakase-only room, two seatings Wed–Sun — the quiet-date splurge closest to downtown.
Convoy's 12-seat omakase gallery — 18 pieces in 90 minutes (~$144) with fish flown from Toyosu; book 60 days out.
Bankers Hill neighborhood favorite bridging date-night polish and honest nigiri — the happy medium under the omakase tier.
Chef Davin Waite's punk-rock Oceanside counter — zero-waste omakase that's a legit destination up the coast.
Tohoku-born, Michelin-listed noodle shop — the tonkotsu that ended the 'SD has no ramen' argument; expect a line.
Convoy's Michelin-recommended home-style izakaya — obanzai small plates and a sake list built for lingering.
Hidden in the Nijiya plaza off Convoy — grilled fish collars, uni bowls, and regulars at the counter; feels like Osaka.
Convoy's homey Korean standby since 2005 — village-style stews, KBBQ, and banchan that keeps coming.
All-you-can-eat Korean BBQ on Convoy (~$30–35 premium tier) — spicy bulgogi, pork belly, and a loud, fun room.
Double-fried Korean chicken, tteokbokki, and cold beer towers — the Convoy group-hang default.
Convoy's upscale AYCE wagyu shabu newcomer in the old Shancheng Lameizi space — tiers roughly $45–98 a head.

chinese.s: Convoy's chile-and-peppercorn workhorse — boiled fish in roiling red oil and dry-fried green beans done right.
No-frills Convoy Sichuan since the 90s — cumin lamb and mapo tofu with real málà burn; bring friends and order big.
Hand-pulled biang biang noodles and cumin-lamb 'Chinese burgers' from an open kitchen — Northwest China on Convoy.
Family-run since 1994 — handmade xiao long bao and potstickers up front, a whiskey-and-craft-beer saloon in back.
The last push-cart dim sum in San Diego — weekend har gow and siu mai the old Hong Kong banquet-hall way.
Back on Convoy after the fire with a full renovation — all-you-can-eat dim sum ordered fresh off the menu.
Big Cantonese banquet room on south Convoy — live-tank seafood dinners and a long-running dim sum service.
Chongqing hot-pot chain on Convoy — split the pot mild/málà, order the butter beef, and settle in for two hours.
The Taiwanese soup-dumpling institution at Westfield UTC — join the waitlist, watch the glass dumpling lab while you wait.
The Convoy-district anchor grocery — live seafood, roast duck, and a plaza ringed with boba shops; stock your pantry.
Cavernous pan-Asian market on Balboa Ave — produce, banchan, and a food-court detour that derails every quick trip.

chinese.n: San Diego Chinese Historical Museum 中华历史博物馆
chinese.s: Downtown's original Chinese Mission building — the story of SD's Chinatown, plus a classical garden out back.
One of Balboa Park's International Cottages — Sunday lawn programs, tea, and volunteers happy to talk 中文 with you.

chinese.n: San Diego Chinese New Year Fair 春节庙会
chinese.s: Annual Lunar New Year street fair (late Jan–Feb) around Third Ave's historic Chinatown — lion dances, food stalls, calligraphy.
Convoy's huge free summer night market — 50+ Asian street-food vendors, DJs, and a beer garden; dates drop at sdnightmarket.com.

fishing.s: The West Coast's oldest landing (1935) — ½-day bay-and-kelp trips to 3-day tuna runs; the easiest on-ramp to SD's famous fleet.
HQ of the long-range tuna fleet — 1.5-day yellowtail to 16-day Guadalupe trips; Coronado Islands runs need a passport and Mexican permits (sold at the landing).
Third of the Scott St landings — solid ½- and ¾-day boats for rockfish, calico bass, and seasonal yellowtail.
Mission Bay's landing — ½-day trips from ~$75 and summer twilight runs; the budget-friendly way to get on fish fast.
License-free public pier minutes from downtown — bay bass, halibut, and bonito runs with the sportfishing fleet parading past.
Fish over the surf line off Pacific Beach's cottage-topped pier — open to the public daytime; no license needed on public piers.
One of the West Coast's longest wooden piers — most of it reopened after the 2024 fire; license-free and productive at dawn.
Sleeper pier in the South Bay — halibut, corbina, and croaker with none of the tourist crush; license-free like all public piers.
Walkable-from-Gaslamp public fishing pier behind the Convention Center — mackerel, bass, and skyline views; license-free.
Spotted bay bass around eelgrass, docks, and channel edges — deadly on small swimbaits; CA license required from shore.

fishing.n: San Diego Bay (Bayside Park, Chula Vista)
fishing.s: The spotted bay bass capital — work the riprap and pilings on a moving tide; kayak launch right there; license from shore.
Dawn-patrol corbina and surfperch on sand crabs along miles of open beach — you need a CA license on the sand, unlike the piers.
City reservoir with winter-stocked trout and year-round largemouth — easy bank access off the paved loop; CA license required.

biking.s: 8,000 acres 20 minutes from downtown — punchy Fortuna climbs, rocky descents, and enough trail to fill a season.
Fast, swoopy singletrack ringing a 1,554-ft summit in Rancho Peñasquitos — the locals' after-work hot lap.
Seven flowy canyon miles to a year-round waterfall — smooth enough for a fitness spin, fun enough to repeat.
Rolling lake-edge singletrack under the I-15 footbridge — big views, rocky ribbons, and post-ride tacos in Rancho Bernardo.
The county's classic: ~10 miles of alpine-to-desert singletrack dropping off the Lagunas near Pine Valley — worth the hour east; shuttle it or earn it.
County-built jump lines, flow trails, and pump track in Bonita — free entry, progression-friendly, closed only for rain and maintenance.
~12 flat bayfront miles looping Mission Bay with a boardwalk spur — the sunset cruiser ride, zero traffic stress.
24-mile bay loop via the Silver Strand — ferry across, spin past the Del, and roll back along the South Bay salt flats.

About 20 miles of fire road, double-track and groomed singletrack in Escondido — gentler routes on the west side, steeper fun singletrack in the east, and a flat meadow loop. Expect a climb to start and lots of hikers.
Advanced singletrack with about 1,600 ft of climbing: start up The Way Up for a technical climb (or the Del Dios side for a grind), then Equine Incline and the Lake Hodges Overlook.

social.s: The Gaslamp's Latin institution — beginner-friendly salsa/bachata lessons most nights, then the floor fills till close.
Salsa and bachata classes seven days a week from a champion team — free Saturday intro class, socials with the same crowd.
San Diego's biggest weekly swing night since 1998, now at Champion Ballroom — lesson included, rotate partners, zero pressure.
Free, hug-heavy 6:29am workout at Balboa Park's Bea Evenson Fountain — the fastest way to meet 100 friendly strangers.
Free 5k/5-mi group run from the North Park shop, all paces welcome — most stick around after; PB edition Mondays.
Newport Ave closes for produce, street food, and live bands with the sunset two blocks away — OB at its friendliest.
Gilbert Castellanos hosts young jazz prodigies then an open jam at Balboa Park — free, all ages, and easy to strike up conversation.

social.n: Chinese Language & Culture Exchange 聖地牙哥中美交流會
social.s: Long-running Mandarin–English meetup — half the room practicing 中文, half English; genuinely conversational by design.
Drop-in beginner/intermediate clinics on the South Mission courts — coached, rotating teams, instant weekend crew.
Downtown's easygoing Wednesday pub quiz with Resident's house beers — teams of strangers welcome; walkable from Gaslamp.
Miramar's huge friendly game store — open tables daily and a full calendar of learn-to-play nights; easiest cold-join in town.
Saturdays from 9a with Social Soccer on Mission Bay - San Diego,California at 1600 Vacation Rd, San Diego, CA 92109 · no Meetup fee.
Saturdays from 8:45a with Balboa Park Saturday Morning Soccer at Balboa Park Information, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Sunday Pickup Soccer in River Park
social.s: This group is not for beginners, however. We’ll try to get a field right behind the kids playground. We use the 4' goals and enjoy a casual pickup game. Sundays from 8a with Sunday Soccer In River Park at Snapdragon / SDSU Mission Valley River Park, San Diego · no Meetup fee.
Fridays from 5p with San Diego Under The Lights Pick-Up Soccer Meet at North Park Recreation Center, San Diego · no Meetup fee.
Every Sunday, start 3:30 pm sharp. All levels & co-ed. Sundays from 3:30p with Coronado Soccer at sunset park, coronado, ca · no Meetup fee.

This week we'll be running out of PB Pub, a straightforward dive bar for us to enjoy after our run. For tonight's route we are tackling a 3.93 mile route. Wednesdays from 7p with SD Fun Run at PB PUB, San Diego · no Meetup fee.
Saturdays from 1p with Mission Bay Co-ed Volleyball at East Mission Bay - Playa Pacifica I and Playa Pacifica II, San Diego · no Meetup fee.
Tuesdays from 5:30p with San Diego Mountain Biking Association (sdmba) at Morley Field Sports Complex, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

Join us for an evening of indoor rock climbing/bouldering! All ages, shapes, sizes, and fitness levels are encouraged to come give it a try. Wednesdays from 6:30p with Sunday Assembly San Diego at Grotto Climbing & Yoga, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

Kizomba is a partner dance often described as “African Tango,” but has its own distinct rich history originating from Angola. Mondays from 7p with The San Diego Salsa Crazy Meetup Group at Tango Del Rey, San Diego · $15 on Meetup.

social.n: FREE Intro to Salsa and Bachata
social.s: Free intro class. Sundays from 12p with Melomano Latin Entertainment & Dance at Melómano Entertainment - Salsa & Bachata Lessons, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

Sunday Salsa On2 Level 1 Class. Designed for people at the beginning of their dance journey and/or reinforcing fundamental Salsa principles. No partner necessary; all students rotate. Class is $20. Sundays from 1p with Melomano Latin Entertainment & Dance at Melómano Entertainment - Salsa & Bachata Lessons, San Diego · $20 on Meetup.

social.n: Oshaberi Tuesday / おしゃべり火曜 / Japan & Japanese Talk
social.s: Every week, we get together for an informal session, where you can come to practice English or Japanese, socialize about culture, study, or just sit back and relax. Tuesdays from 6p with Japanese Language & Culture Exchange of San Diego 日本人と外人集まる会 at Tea N More, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Beginner LINE DANCING & Swing - Silvergate in North Park
social.s: Come on out and learn some line dancing with a great group of beginners...alongside Philip Victor (aka BootScootin), a nationally renowned instructor & emcee. Mondays from 6:30p with ¡ ᗯᗩᑎTEᗪ TO ᗪO TᕼᗩT . . . ᒍᑌᔕT ᑎOT ᗩᒪOᑎE ! ! ! ℠ San Diego at Silvergate Three Stars Masonic, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Thursday We Dance At Tango Del Rey 50/50 Salsa & Bachata
social.s: Thursdays from 8p with San Diego Salsa Bachata Latin Dancing Meet UP at Tango Del Rey, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

social.n: TdR-Salsa Bachata at Tango Del Rey
social.s: Thursdays from 8:30p with The San Diego Salsa Crazy Meetup Group at Tango Del Rey, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Learn the art of TAIKO - Japanese Drumming
social.s: Whether you are new in town or a long-time resident, this event offers a unique opportunity to connect with others who share a passion and respect for Asian culture and percussion music. Sundays from 10a with TAIKO: The Art of Japanese Drumming in San Diego [太鼓] at 2971 India St., San Diego · no Meetup fee.

social.n: TCSD Beginner Triathlon Workout (Run, Cycle, Swim)
social.s: The distances you choose to run,cycle and swim are based on your goals. Sundays from 6:30a with San Diego Triathlon Series Free Training Clinics & Events at Glorietta Bay Park, Coronado · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: Local operator on the 4th floor of 550 W B St at India, between the Gaslamp and Little Italy. Fiber Wi-Fi, extra-large phone booths, a kitchen with coffee, tea and craft beer on tap, a roof deck with bay views, outdoor workspaces and a podcast room. Members get printing (up to 1,000 b&w/500 color pages a mo); open-desk members get 24/7 access. Day pass M–F 8a–5p.
remote.p: $40 day pass (5- & 10-day bundles from $30/day) · $195/mo (10 days) · $295/mo unlimited
remote.b: Social space plus quiet areas; music can play loud during focus hours

remote.s: 10,000 sq ft beach-side branch at 4438 Ingraham St, a 10-min walk to Pacific and Mission Beach — with free street parking. Fiber internet, big phone booths, meeting rooms with video conferencing, an outdoor patio, coffee & tea, monthly printing, a weekly happy hour and dogs welcome. Day pass M–F 8a–5p.
remote.p: $40 day pass (bundles from $30/day) · memberships, offices & hourly rooms
remote.b: Open floor quiet most days, but common-area noise carries; phone booths in demand

remote.s: Downtown WeWork in the 600 B St tower, a few blocks north of the Gaslamp. High-speed Wi-Fi, phone booths, business-class printers, meeting rooms and staffed reception, plus an espresso bar, bike storage, showers, a wellness room and dog-friendly floors. A membership also opens WeWork Aventine in La Jolla.
remote.p: Day pass from $39 · coworking from $289/mo · dedicated desk from $314/mo
remote.b: Big outdoor terrace with plenty of room to sit and work

remote.s: Independent coworking at 3919 30th St in the middle of North Park's bar-and-coffee strip. High-speed Wi-Fi, coffee & tea, phone booths, conference rooms, printer/scanner and bike storage, plus community events and neighborhood discounts. Staffed M–F 8a–4p; members get 24/7 access, and dedicated desks add the other California locations.
remote.p: $35 day pass · flex desk $400/mo · dedicated desk $650/mo
remote.b: Busy and small, but reviewers say there is enough room; few call rooms

remote.s: The domed nine-story library at 330 Park Blvd in East Village, two blocks from Petco Park. Free Wi-Fi with no card or session limit (until 15 min before close) and wireless printing from your laptop via Princh. Mon–Tue 11:30–8, Wed–Fri 9:30–6, Sat 10–4, closed Sun. Garage: first 2 hr free with lobby validation, then $1.25/20 min ($21 max). Trolley to Park & Market.
remote.b: Upper floors like the 8th are quietest; private study rooms available

remote.s: Bright 2019 branch at 215 W Washington St, between Mission Hills and Hillcrest, with study rooms, computer labs, Wi-Fi and a community meeting space. Underground garage: first 2 hr free with validation, then $1.25/20 min. Tue 11:30–8, Wed–Sat 9:30–6; closed Sun–Mon.
remote.b: Peaceful most of the time; occasional noise from staff activities

remote.s: University Heights institution at 4496 Park Blvd, open 24 hours, with couches and a steady crowd of students studying — the answer when you need to work at 2 a.m.
remote.b: Quiet back room for late-night study; can get crowded at peak times

remote.s: Ocean Beach coffee bar at 4810 Santa Monica Ave that The Infatuation rates as a genuinely good workspace — indoor seating and enough chargers to go around.
Student-favorite café at 5900 El Cajon Blvd by SDSU, tagged for getting work done, with an outdoor patio and hours until 11p daily.
remote.b: SDSU students fill tables in the afternoon; quieter corners upstairs

events.n: Teddy Swims: The UGLY Tour
events.s: The soul-pop powerhouse brings his arena tour to Pechanga Arena in the Midway District.

events.n: Jo Koy: Koy Meets World Tour
events.s: The Filipino-American stand-up headlines the San Diego Civic Theatre downtown.

events.n: Skating by the Sea at Hotel del Coronado
events.s: An oceanfront ice rink on the Del's beach, open daily through the holidays (10a–10p on weekends and from 12/18 on). Pair it with a sunset walk on Coronado Beach.

events.n: San Diego Gulls vs. Ontario Reign
events.s: AHL hockey at Pechanga Arena: the Ducks' affiliate hosts the Kings' farm team on Thanksgiving week. Doors at 6p.

events.n: December Nights in Balboa Park
events.s: The city's biggest free holiday festival. Museums open free in the evening, and you'll find food vendors, holiday décor and a beer & sake garden at the Japanese Friendship Garden.

events.n: Victoria Monét: Frequency of Love Tour
events.s: The Grammy-winning R&B singer plays the outdoor Cal Coast Credit Union Open Air Theatre at SDSU.

events.n: San Diego Bay Parade of Lights
events.s: Lit-up boats parade along the bayfront toward Coronado on two Sundays only, 12/13 and 12/20, starting at 5:30p. This year's theme is "Liberty Lights the Bay." Free to watch from the waterfront.

events.n: Jungle Bells at the San Diego Zoo
events.s: The zoo stays open late for the holidays: light treks, a Holiday Forest and a light-and-symphony show from 5p until 8p close. Closed 12/24.

events.n: Holiday Bowl
events.s: The 47th Holiday Bowl at Snapdragon Stadium: an ACC team vs. a team from the former Pac-12 conference.

events.n: Disney's The Lion King
events.s: The Broadway blockbuster's three-week run at the Civic Theatre. Tickets go on sale 11/13.

events.n: Jimmy O. Yang: Has No Friends Tour
events.s: The Hong Kong–born comedian (Silicon Valley, Interior Chinatown) brings his new hour to the Civic Theatre.

events.n: Syd: Beard Tour
events.s: The Internet's former frontwoman brings her neo-soul and alt-R&B album Beard to the 1,100-capacity Observatory North Park, a historic University Ave theater.

events.n: Chris Fleming Live
events.s: The Emmy-nominated cult favorite brings his absurdist, high-energy stand-up to the restored 1920s Balboa Theatre in the Gaslamp.

events.n: San Diego Gulls vs. Iowa Wild
events.s: A Saturday-evening AHL matchup at Pechanga Arena closing out a two-game weekend set against Minnesota's top affiliate. Doors at 5p.

events.n: Dr. Seuss's How the Grinch Stole Christmas! at The Old Globe
events.s: San Diego's holiday-stage tradition returns to the Globe's Shiley Stage in Balboa Park, with 10:30a all-ages matinees for families and evening shows most nights.

events.n: SDSU Aztecs vs. UNLV (men's basketball)
events.s: Mountain West rivals UNLV visit Viejas Arena on campus for a Saturday-afternoon tip, one of the marquee dates on the Aztecs' December home slate.

events.n: Little Italy Tree Lighting & Christmas Village
events.s: India Street fills with artisan stalls, live music and Santa, building to a traditional Italian lighting of the 25-foot tree in Piazza della Famiglia at 6:30p.

events.n: Golden State Ballet: The Nutcracker
events.s: Raúl Salamanca's staging at the Civic Theatre downtown, with the San Diego Symphony playing Tchaikovsky's score live. Matinee and evening shows run through the 23rd.

events.n: Sunday Beginner-friendly Coed Soccer!
events.s: Balls shot at goal are to be ground to waist level of keeper and not shot at full force. All kicks higher than opposing player’s waist are not allowed. Sunday from 8a with Casual Coed Soccer at Snapdragon / SDSU Mission Valley River Park, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Beginner Beach Volleyball
events.s: This event is only for beginners. Join us on Instagram & Facebook & Messenger. Sunday from 3p with Fun Times in San Diego at Coronado Beach · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Joshua Tree National Park Day Trip
events.s: Sunday from 8a with Sunday Hike San Diego at Starbucks, 789 W Harbor Dr, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Hiking Annie's Canyon Trail
events.s: Friday from 8a with Sunday Hike San Diego at Starbucks, 789 W Harbor Dr, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: FREE Multi-groups Local Urban Trail Hike- Marian Bear Park ~ 4 miles
events.s: Relatively easy mostly flat trail hike after initial short steep access down from the cul-de-sac at North end of Biltmore St. Saturday from 1p with San Diego Day Hikers at Marian Bear Park meet at Biltmore St access trailhead post, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Chollas Lake Wildlife and Ethnobotany Walk
events.s: Join a Park Naturalist Lauren to discover native wildlife at Chollas Lake Park. She will also discuss how native plants are used by indigenous peoples on this easy, 1-mile walk. Saturday from 1p with San Diego Day Hikers at Chollas Lake Park, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Meet new people downtown, enjoy some free offerings and stay to play trivia
events.s: Come out and meet new people. Tuesday from 6p with San Diego/Gaslamp Martini Club at Wild Hare Bar Garden, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Karaoke Bash - Private space for singles bash!
events.s: Step out from behind the screen and into a real night out! Join us for an exclusive, private singles party packed with great tunes, good energy, and actual human connection. MC will guide us through the night. Friday from 7p with PopSpot Singles and Socials Mingle at Indya Restaurant & Bar, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: [RideSD] Transit Happy Hour
events.s: Join RideSD for their monthly transit happy hour. Tuesday from 6p with San Diego Urbanism at Hidden Craft, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Mindful Taiko: Mindfulness Experience Through Japanese Taiko
events.s: Saturday from 1p with Mindful Taiko: Mindfulness Experience Through Japanese Taiko at The Block Club, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Board Game Night at Rocko's Modern Taphouse
events.s: The Hoppy Dice is bringing game night to Rocko's Modern Taphouse! Still 20+ board games, endless fun, and great beer and food! The best part remains: you decide what your game night looks like! Thursday from 6p with The Hoppy Dice Board Game Nights! at Rocko's Modern Taphouse, San Diego · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Mahjong @ San Diego Anime Con
events.s: Learn to Play Mahjong with San Diego Mahjong Club! Saturday from 10a with San Diego Mahjong Club at DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley · no Meetup fee.

iceskating.s: The Del's oceanfront rink on the Windsor Lawn runs daily Nov 20, 2026–Jan 3, 2027, from 10a–10p on weekends and every day from Dec 18. Tickets are $40–45 for a 90-minute session, with $35 value sessions on select mornings, and skates are included. Military, members and hotel guests get $5 off. Buy online ahead.

iceskating.n: Rady Children's Ice Rink at Liberty Station
iceskating.s: A seasonal outdoor rink on Legacy Plaza at Liberty Station, open Nov 19, 2026–Jan 3, 2027, daily 10a–10p in three sessions with Zamboni breaks at 5 and 7:30p. It's $20 adult and $15 child through Dec 20, then $30 and $20, with skates and helmets included. Proceeds go to Rady Children's Thriving After Cancer program.

An outdoor rink at the Viejas Outlet Center in Alpine, out in East County. It's open Nov 6, 2026–Jan 10, 2027, daily 3–10p, weather permitting, and closed Thanksgiving, with short hours on the holidays. It's $24 for 13 and up and $22 for 12 and under, and that covers a 90-minute session with rental skates.

The Salvation Army Kroc Center's rink on University Ave, the only year-round ice arena in central San Diego. Public skate is $25 with skates ($20 for members), and it's $5 less bought online 48 hours ahead. Session times shift with programs, so check the hours page. Text SDKROC for same-day closures.

The rink inside the open-air Westfield UTC mall in University City, at 4545 La Jolla Village Dr. It runs daily public sessions, sold as a one-day pass or an annual unlimited public pass, and has a pro shop and skate sharpening. Skate, then eat at the mall. Session times are on the rink's schedule page.

Mira Mesa's rink at 11048 Ice Skate Place, running since 1978, with daily public skating plus lessons, hockey leagues and a pro shop. Session times and prices aren't on the home page, so call 858-530-1825 to confirm before driving up.

The Rinks' North County rink off Scripps Poway Pkwy, at 12455 Kerran St, with daily public sessions. Admission is $18 plus $8 rental. Walk-ins are welcome, or buy online until an hour before (it needs a DaySmart account). Weekend sessions may pause 10 minutes for resurfacing, and Skate Mates are available for beginners.

skating.s: The 3-mile concrete Ocean Front Walk from the South Mission jetty to Pacific Beach is open to inline skaters, but speed is capped at 8 mph and the foot traffic is heavy, so it's a cruise rather than a workout. A 2025 reviewer rates it great for skating and people-watching. Belmont Park and its coaster sit midway.

An 11.6-mile heart-shaped paved loop around Mission Bay. It's broad and car-free apart from a sidewalk stretch on East Mission Bay Dr. A roller skater who reviewed it in 2024 called it well maintained and fine for skating, though beginners should watch the expansion joints and drifted sand. E-bikes are banned, and it gets busier on weekends.

The flat bayfront promenade a short roll from the Gaslamp. Starting from Seaport Village or the Rady Shell, skate north past the ships to Harbor Island and back, about 8 miles round trip. It's flat and on the water the whole way, and shared with walkers, so expect to weave near Seaport Village and the Midway.

Take the ferry to Coronado Ferry Landing and skate south. The west side of the 24-mile Bayshore Bikeway is a separate paved path down the Silver Strand toward Imperial Beach, scenic and with no shade. There's one on-street stretch near 10th St and Glorietta Blvd. Reviewers skip the east side, which is mostly on-street and poorly marked.

Flat, newer concrete beside the coastal rail line, about 3 miles out and back between Chesterfield Dr in Cardiff and Santa Fe Dr in Encinitas. This segment opened in 2019. It's the North County pick for a smooth, flat skate between the beach towns, with the ocean a block or two west.

In Point Loma, there's an open concrete plaza (the ice rink's footprint in winter) plus a paved waterfront path of about a mile. It's free and open at any hour, and local roller groups run free lessons and meetups here. From Nov 19 to Jan 3 the holiday ice rink takes over part of the plaza.

Ocean Beach's city skatepark at 2525 Bacon St: about 40,000 sq ft of concrete with a street course and a bowl, and a smooth path around the outside. It's open 10a to dusk daily. City skatepark rules allow inline skates and roller skates but require a helmet plus elbow and knee pads, and kids under 12 need a parent.

Linda Vista's indoor roller rink, open since 1975. All-ages sessions run Thu 5–8p, Fri 5–10p, Sat 11a–10p and Sun noon–8:30p, at $18 for three hours plus $7 rental, and Wednesday family night is $10. 18+ nights run Tue (intermediate and up) and Thu 8:30–11p, and there's an 18+ lunch skate Tue and Thu 10a–noon.

skating.n: Ringer's Roller Rink at Seaport Village
skating.s: A shaded open-air roller rink at Seaport Village, a short roll from the Gaslamp, that opened in 2026. Public skating runs daily 10a–9p at $18. Quad rentals are $6, pads and a helmet $8, and a Skate Mate $10. Inline rentals aren't listed, so bring your own blades. The original Ringer's on Federal Blvd skates Thu–Sun.

A 600-plus-member Meetup of urban inline skaters with Thursday-evening group skates on alternating weeks. One is Harbor Island to downtown for drinks: about 12 miles, advanced, over rough streets and rail crossings. The other is Crown Point to Mission Beach, with 4–20 mile route options including an easy boardwalk skate. Bring lights for the ride back.
